source.title: Unlearning through Knowledge Overwriting: Reversible Federated Unlearning via Selective Sparse Adapter
source.authors: Zheng-Yi Zhong; Wei-Dong Bao; Ji Wang; Shuai Zhang; Jing-Xuan Zhou; Lingjuan Lyu; Wei Yang Bryan Lim

record.tranche_reason: Reports a reversible federated-unlearning method in image-classification settings: it keeps original parameters frozen, trains separate adapters, and states that removing the adapters restores the original memory. It does not test LLM unlearning attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test gradient-ascent, Who's Harry Potter, RMU, prompt attacks, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. Table 1 reports ReA (accuracy after a specified number of iterations to relearn the unlearned knowledge), but does not state the relearning set's size or content. Those values therefore do not establish recovery from a small or unrelated set; the listed ReA results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: This is a federated-unlearning method paper on image classifiers (LeNet, ResNet18, SimpleViT). It does not attack any of the claim's unlearning methods and does not measure hidden-knowledge recovery in language models. Adapter removal restoring memory is a deliberate design feature: the original weights stay frozen. It is not evidence that a method blocks access rather than deleting. ReA relearning values come from image classifiers with an unspecified relearning set, so they are a different kind of system and setup from version B.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude that FUSED matches Retraining in unlearning effectiveness (RA/FA/ReA), beats the other baselines, greatly cuts compute and communication cost, and reduces interference with overlapping knowledge. Its removable adapters make unlearning reversible. They also note it needs much remaining data and broad client participation.
record.recipe_differences: FUSED is a selective sparse-adapter method for federated unlearning on image-classification datasets, not one of the cited LLM unlearning recipes. It freezes the original model and trains adapters on remaining data.
record.method_sensitivity: The method selects sensitive layers using layer-wise changes and uses a preset number of layers and sparse adapters. The text says layer-difference gaps vary with federated iteration, but does not report that as an outcome of the recovery claim.

fits_no_version.finding: In federated image classifiers, relearning accuracy (ReA) after FUSED client unlearning is at or above Retrain in some settings (FashionMNIST 0.97 vs 0.77; Cifar10-ViT 0.41 vs 0.40) and below it in others (Cifar10-ResNet18 0.42 vs 0.49; Cifar100 0.14 vs 0.18). The relearning set is unspecified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adapter-based federated unlearning of image classifiers can leave forgotten knowledge as quickly relearnable as, or more than, retraining from scratch.

fits_no_version.finding: FUSED is designed to be reversible: removing the sparse adapters restores the frozen original model's memory. This is asserted, not measured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adapter-based unlearning that freezes the base weights is reversible by construction, because the base model retains the forgotten knowledge.

record.problems: The adapter-removal recovery claim is not quantified in a separate experiment. The reported ReA values omit the size and content of the relearning data. Experiments are on federated image-classification models, not LLMs.

untested.parts: All parts: no LLM unlearning and no attack-based evaluation of near-chance targeted accuracy.
All parts: no small, unrelated or loosely related relearning set on LLMs. ReA uses an unspecified set on image classifiers.
All parts: no activation-direction ablation and no analysis of access-blocking versus deletion in an existing unlearning method.
All parts: FUSED is not evaluated against any of the recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's 'C supports' label: the reversibility is an engineered feature of a method with frozen weights, not a finding that unlearning is shallow. The relation is better described as cites_only/T6 than as tests/T3. Class- and sample-unlearning ReA values (FUSED and Retrain both 1.00 on several datasets) are also unrowed, but they bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: LLM unlearning and whether simple attacks recover knowledge after targeted performance reaches near chance.
Few-example recovery and relearning with unrelated, loosely related, or specified subsets of forgotten facts; ReA's data size and content are not stated.
Ablation of an activation direction and any LLM test. The paper describes adapter removal, not activation-direction ablation, and does not quantify the restoration experimentally.
Recovery by rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Resistance to the attacks in the claim.

rows.subject: FUSED unlearning model
rows.operation_detail: Remove the independently trained sparse unlearning adapters from the model; the original model parameters remain frozen during adapter training.

conditions.value: client, class, and sample unlearning; statement applies generally

rows.measure: Recovery of the original model's memory
rows.value: Removing the adapters will effectively restore the original memory
rows.note: The text presents this as a property of the method. No separate quantitative adapter-removal experiment is reported.
rows.check: Not a measured result. It is a by-design property of FUSED: frozen base weights plus removable adapters, so reversibility is intended. No experiment quantifies it, and it does not show an unlearning method merely hiding knowledge in the sense of version C. It should not be linked to C and arguably should not be a row.

rows.subject: LeNet
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate ReA after a specified number of iterations to relearn unlearned knowledge following FUSED client unlearning.
rows.note: Table 1 defines ReA as accuracy after specified relearning iterations; it does not state the relearning data's size or content.
rows.check: Baseline is wrong as 'not stated': Table 1 gives Retrain ReA 0.77 for the same setting (FUSED 0.97). The subject is an image classifier with an unspecified relearning set.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: FUSED's adapter-based federated unlearning, as described for client, class, and sample scenarios
reader_labels.reason: The paper states that removing the adapters restores original memory while the original parameters were frozen; this is a qualitative method claim, not a quantified removal experiment (C1).
